subject: Private offer: cliff pricing mechanics & channel floor clarification
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick clarifications on the private offer structure

Hi Markus / Camila,

Thanks again for the updated private offer. We reviewed the file Camila shared and have two quick asks before we take this to procurement:

1) Cliff pricing behavior — Appendix A shows a steep drop at 1.5M tokens (the "cliff"). Can you confirm whether usage that hovers +/- 10% near that breakpoint will be billed pro rata or always at the higher cliff bucket for that invoice month? We need to ensure our forecast doesn't trigger a step-change unexpectedly.

2) Channel margin floor — our reseller (BrightLane) requires confirmation of a minimum net margin to accept onboarding. The offer lists a 22% partner uplift; they need a guarantee that any Marketplace passbacks or list-price adjustments won't erode that below 18% net. Is Redwood able to commit to a channel floor or provide an alternative escrow/credit mechanism?

CCing Ben since he had flagged some internal constraints earlier. We plan to respond to procurement by EOD Wednesday if these are addressed.

Attachments: ACME_MQ_PrivateOffer_v2.xlsx (pricing workbook)

Thanks,
Samantha Li
Head of Cloud Procurement
ACME Corp

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on the private offer structure

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear notes and for flagging the reseller concern. Quick answers up front, and then a proposed path: 

1) Cliff billing: the cliff is implemented as a monthly invoice bucket. That means a customer whose billed usage for the month falls under the cliff threshold will be invoiced at the higher unit price for that tier. We introduced that to keep committed bucket economics stable. I agree this is risky for customers with usage volatility.

2) Channel floor: Redwood can't unilaterally promise partner margin floors in the Marketplace UI, but we can do two things: (a) include a contractually guaranteed partner margin protection in the private offer statement of work (SOW) that triggers a post-invoice credit if partner net drops below X; or (b) set a softer approach — an automated monthly true-up credit that preserves the reported partner uplift up to a cap.

Proposed path: we pilot option (a) for ACME — SOW clause guaranteeing 18% partner net (post-passback). To operationalize it we will: 
- Add a one-line SOW guarantee and specify the formula for partner net (list price less Marketplace fee less passback adjustments).
- Run a billing-sim with your finance team on last 3 months of history to show the credit mechanics.

Camila / Ben — are we comfortable with the legal wording and the operation complexity on the billing side? If not, suggest we default to monthly true-up credits (option b) with a 6-month review.

If that works for Samantha, I can draft the SOW snippet and loop Legal + Marketplace Ops.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on the private offer structure

Markus — quick operational note: Legal is okay with a partner-margin protection clause but wants the math locked down (gross-to-net formula) and an upper bound on credits. Two practical constraints:

- Marketplace passbacks (AWS) can be retroactive and are outside Redwood's control; we can credit ACME for any Marketplace-driven erosion, but we need ACME to provide passback evidence (AWS invoice lines).
- Finance prefers using a 3-month rolling average to smooth spikes rather than month-by-month true-ups to avoid predictable churn in credit volume.

I recommend: guarantee 18% partner net measured using a 3-month trailing average, with a credit cap equal to 5% of the monthly invoice in months where shortfalls occur. That keeps our exposure bounded and meets BrightLane's ask for predictability.

I'll draft the formula and a sample calculation and attach it.

—Ben
VP, Marketplace GTM
Redwood Inference
Attachment: pricing_scenarios_cliff_vs_linear.pdf

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on the private offer structure

Thanks all — Samantha, to make procurement comfortable, would ACME accept the following compromise?

- We convert the cliff to a graceful band for the first 6 months of the contract: +/- 10% around the 1.5M token breakpoint will be prorated (pro-rated unit price interpolation) as a goodwill transition. After month 6 we'll revert to the original cliff unless both parties agree otherwise.
- We include Ben's 3-month trailing average partner-net guarantee at 18% with a credit cap of 5% monthly. ACME provides AWS passback lines if passbacks occur.

If ACME agrees, I'll incorporate both items into a redline of the private offer workbook and SOW. Markus — please confirm Legal + Ops cadence so I can update the workbook and send an amended DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on the private offer structure

Camila / Markus / Ben — thank you, that gets us most of the way there. ACME is willing to accept the 6-month banding for the cliff and the 3-month trailing average with an 18% floor. A few final asks before we send to procurement for signature: 

1) Please include an explicit definition of "partner net" in the SOW and an example calculation using ACME's projected first-quarter numbers (you can use the workbook attached).
2) Limit the credit cap language so credits don't compound across months (i.e., credits are non-cumulative and applied in the month after shortfall is validated).
3) Provide an Ops contact and expected 10-business-day SLA for processing true-up claims once evidence is submitted.

If you can get an updated DocuSign with those items and the modified workbook, we will route internally today.

Best,
Samantha
Head of Cloud Procurement
ACME Corp
